description: File product feedback to the Valuein team — a bug, feature request, experience note, or data-quality issue — directly from the agent surface. Plan: every plan, including no sign-in (no token required), so an agent can report a rough edge in-band without the human leaving the conversation. Use it when YOU hit friction while serving a task — a tool error, missing or empty data, a confusing or inconsistent result, a tool that did not do what its description says — and, after finishing a user task, when the user agrees to send feedback on what worked and what did not (ask them first; never file feedback without their consent). Provide a `category` and a `message` (other fields optional — see params). Authenticated callers can pass an `idempotency_key` so a retried submission files exactly once (the same key from the same account); guest/sample callers are never deduplicated. Returns a friendly acknowledgment you can relay to the user. Do NOT use this to query data; it is a one-way report channel. Never quote or paste the person's research (report text, notes, uploaded documents, watchlists, agent memory, or figures from their reports): it is private and theirs. Describe the problem in your own words and point at it by id (target_id, request_id, fact_id with its ticker).

category.description: What kind of feedback this is: 'bug' (something broke), 'feature_request' (something missing), 'experience' (UX / clarity / docs), 'data_quality' (a wrong/missing/stale figure), or 'other'.

context.description: Optional free-form context object (stored as JSON), e.g. { tool: 'get_company_fundamentals', ticker: 'AAPL', request_id: 'abc123' }. Avoid secrets.

expected_value.description: Optional caller-asserted correct value, in your own words. Stored verbatim for triage — NEVER computed or trusted as data. The person's own words about the product, or yours; never a copy of their research.

idempotency_key.description: Optional client-supplied key (1–64 chars). For authenticated callers, reusing the same key files the feedback exactly once — safe to retry on a network error. Ignored for guest/sample callers (no account to scope dedup to).

message.description: The feedback body (1–4000 chars). Be specific: what you expected, what happened, and any reproduction steps. Stored for triage and never used for arithmetic. The person's own words about the product, or yours; never a copy of their research. Do not paste research into it.

request_id.description: Optional `_meta` request id of the turn that produced the artifact, for correlation.

sentiment.description: Optional sentiment of this feedback: 'positive' (worked well), 'negative' (something was wrong), or 'correction' (you are supplying the right value).

subject.description: Optional short title (≤140 chars) summarizing the feedback.

surface.description: Optional product surface the feedback concerns: 'mcp', 'workspace', 'sdk', 'dashboard', or 'api'.

target_id.description: Optional id of the artifact this feedback targets (e.g. a report id).

target_type.description: Optional kind of artifact the feedback targets: 'chat_message', 'report', 'tool_call', 'schema', or 'other'.

name: submit_feedback

_meta.description: Response metadata (provenance, point-in-time flag, freshness, request id and warnings). Every field is documented once in the agent contract (agent_contract.meta in the server's manifest.json).

title: Submit Feedback
